name: GLUE
summary: A historical lunar-radio search used NASA Deep Space Network dishes to look for particle cascades in the Moon, turning the lunar regolith into a vast neutrino target.
detection_principle: A neutrino-induced cascade in lunar material can emit a coherent radio pulse that escapes toward Earth. Coincident detection at separated antennas suppresses terrestrial radio interference.

sites.name: United States; Goldstone Deep Space Communications antennas in California, with the Moon as the target
sites.location: United States; Goldstone Deep Space Communications antennas in California, with the Moon as the target

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The cited publications describe a completed historical observing campaign, not a continuously operating dedicated detector.

results.summary: No convincing lunar neutrino pulse was observed; flux limits constrained ultra-high-energy models.
